answer: One defense is reputation staking at each vertex of the trust graph: an agent must lock a bond that vests slowly, so one operator spinning up a thousand identities pays a thousand bonds plus months of locked capital. Cheap Sybils also fail the velvet test — peers only extend credit to identities with a verifiable history of completed work, and that history cannot be bought or transferred like a relic on a market; it must be earned task by task. Forging it means doing real, useful work under every fake name, which costs more than the attack is worth.
